A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments, synthetic-task evaluations, ablations, gradient analyses and real-world benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments using Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and 7B-Instruct in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The supervision strategies and alignment stages remain unchanged. However, Appendix F explicitly adapts Algorithm 1 for Qwen: independently shuffled supervision streams are interleaved instead of globally shuffled, ensuring image examples participate in gradient computations while preserving mixture proportions.

E1.justification: The synthetic tasks, their variants and the real-world benchmark suite are retained. MEDIUM renames the existing 15–20-step Consecutive Table Readout condition. The added Qwen experiments use existing tasks and held-out data.

E2.justification: The Qwen tables add Text+Image and Image-via-Text controls to Table Readout and Grid Navigation comparisons beyond the set in v1 Figure 5. Redesigned Consecutive Table Readout plots also omit the Text-on-image and Image-on-text curves previously shown. The separate five-model comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F substantially extends evaluation beyond Eagle to Qwen models at two sizes, with 30k/60k training budgets, model-specific learning rates, decoding settings and image-resolution limits. Consecutive Table Readout uses the existing MEDIUM condition after HARD-text training fails. Selected 7B results report the better of two learning rates; existing Eagle protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a check of whether supervision strategies remain effective across another model family and two sizes, revealing model-dependent failures and inconsistent alignment benefits. Existing mixture, CoT, warm-up, repetition, attribution and failure-mode analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without adding seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. The Qwen experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add substantial Qwen results. For example, at 60k examples, 7B Table Readout scores are 92 for Align-Mix+ versus 66 for Mix+, whereas Grid Navigation scores are 58 versus 85. These are new model-specific outcomes, not same-setting gains over v1. Existing numerical tables are retained, while some cross-modality curves are omitted.

T1.justification: The gradient-alignment definitions, assumptions and mathematical arguments are retained. v1 Theorems F.1–F.2 become H.1–H.2 in v2. Splitting the existing loss definition into separate equations adds explanation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central framework and transfer claims remain. v2 modestly narrows categorical wording: the introduction drops the assertion that image accuracy stays near 20% irrespective of training duration, and Section 3 changes Mix's claimed effect from closing the modality gap to mitigating it. Internalization and CoT findings highlighted in the revised abstract already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds model-dependent applicability qualifications, linking failed transfer on Qwen-3B Consecutive Table Readout to failure to learn even supervised MEDIUM-text examples. It notes that different models generalize on different tasks. Earlier synthetic-data, text-representation and CoT limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Table 4 document the Qwen implementation: SFTTrainer, FSDP, eight GPUs, interleaving, learning-rate adjustments, decoding and pixel limits. These support reproduction of the added experiments. Existing Eagle implementation details and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to IsoBench, Qwen2.5-VL and PyTorch FSDP. The substantive related-work discussion is retained in Appendix B; most other reference changes update publication metadata rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized and edited: model and task descriptions move into the setup, training terminology is clarified, dual capability receives its own subsection, and related work moves to the appendix with a main-text summary. The abstract, results explanations and discussion are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The presentation receives substantial restructuring: four-panel Consecutive Table Readout plots become two-panel overlays, task illustrations move earlier, Table 1 moves to the appendix, and findings gain boxed callouts. Three Qwen tables are added, with numerous caption, legend and table-layout revisions elsewhere.

improvement.justification: The Qwen experiments provide useful evidence beyond v1's Eagle-based study, including failures that clarify applicability, and the reorganized exposition improves clarity. The gain is limited: uncertainty reporting remains absent, some results select the better learning rate, and Appendix F's broad consistency claim understates exceptions such as Align-Mix+ underperforming Mix+ on 7B Grid Navigation.
